The rows that break a check

Source: R/violations.R
violations.Rd

A failed checkpoint shows the number of offending rows and the first few of them. violations() returns all of them, to filter, count and look at in the session: wrap the check in it.

Usage

violations(check)

Arguments

check

A call to an ensure_*() checkpoint, or a pipeline of them. In a pipeline the rows of the first check that fails are returned, and the checks after it do not run.

Value

A tibble with the offending rows, key columns first, and the diagnostic column of the check (dupid, overlap_id, outside, reason) where it has one. When every check passes, the data with no rows, and so without a diagnostic column. For a database or Arrow table both are queries: collect() them to get the rows.

Details

dups <- violations(ensure_unique(persons, cpr, year))

It exists so the rows can be had without knowing about conditions. A failed check signals a condition of class inshape_failure that carries the rows (see checkpoints), and catching it by hand has a trap: a tryCatch() around a check that passes returns the whole data, since that is what a checkpoint returns. violations() returns no rows then.

Nothing is printed for a failed check, whether it warns or aborts: the rows are the answer. A check that passes still says so.

The rows are personal data, as they are in the message. They are kept only where you assign them; see Personal data in checkpoints.

See also

checkpoints for the condition and for personal data.

Examples

persons <- data.frame(
  cpr  = c("a", "b", "b", "c"),
  year = c(2024, 2024, 2024, 2024)
)
violations(ensure_unique(persons, cpr, year))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   dupid cpr    year
#>   <int> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1     1 b      2024
#> 2     1 b      2024

# No rows when the check passes
violations(ensure_unique(persons, cpr))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   dupid cpr    year
#>   <int> <chr> <dbl>
#> 1     1 b      2024
#> 2     1 b      2024
